answer: Small tremors ripple through the ground at known speeds, so a device records the arrival time of a micro-tremor, and regional sensors must confirm the same wavefront within its travel-time window. The arrival order is fixed by geology, like water finding a canyon bed, and a yarrow stalk cannot bend the physics: even a faint event carries a distinct ordering, while a marble slab on a distant server feels nothing, so a farm would need real sensors at every claimed site.
